episode_title: Shannon and the Birth of Information, 1948
description: This episode explores Claude Shannon's 1948 paper 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication,' which transformed information from an abstract concept into a measurable physical quantity with fundamental limits. It covers how Shannon defined the bit, established entropy as a measure of information content, proved the limits of data compression and reliable communication through noisy channels, and laid the mathematical foundation for all digital technology. Essential for anyone interested in computer science, telecommunications, cryptography, or the theoretical underpinnings of the digital age.
